input: This summary reviews delivery performance at a contract packaging firm that runs 4 plants and generates revenue of $82 million per year. Drawing on order records for 12 months, covering 11220 orders, on-time delivery over the last two quarters stood at 87%, which falls short of the target of 95%. Late delivery is heavily concentrated: Plant 2 accounts for no less than 52% of late orders, more than the other plants combined. Overtime cost was $2.2 million last year, up 16% on the year before, while the order backlog now stands at 4.1 weeks, compared with 1.9 weeks a year ago. A scheduling system covering all plants is quoted at $346k, with Plant 2 alone quoted at $148k. An internal estimate, which it should be stressed is not a vendor figure, puts the overtime reduction at Plant 2 at 15–20% in the first year. Against this background, the recommendation under consideration is to install the system at Plant 2 first and to hold the other plants until Plant 2 results are reported; the operations director owns the scheduling programme. The trade-off at Plant 2 is the $148k installation against the internally estimated overtime saving. Holding the remaining plants costs no installation spend in the meantime, and it means that the wider decision will depend on measured Plant 2 performance rather than on the estimate alone.
